messages:
lena: Quick heads-up — I ran a dependency scan this morning and flagged CVE-2025-0456 affecting grpc-go 1.57.x and a related oauth/jwt token parsing lib. Proposing a short plan: 1) emergency hotpatch for prod paths, 2) backport to 1.56 branch where feasible, 3) lockfile + verify checks in CI, 4) update KMS usage audit to ensure no token material leaked. Thoughts?

sam: +1. Can you paste the minimal repro / vulnerable import paths?

lena: repro is in the scan report, but quick excerpt: vulnerable path is "google.golang.org/grpc/encoding/proto" transitively importing "github.com/some/jwtlib". Example go.mod snippet:

```
module github.com/redwood/inference

require (
\tgoogle.golang.org/grpc v1.57.2
\tgithub.com/some/jwtlib v0.9.0
)

// pinned in go.sum
```

sam: ok. Are we seeing exploit attempts in logs?

ada: Log query (just ran):
`index=prod_auth severity=warning "jwtlib" OR "proto" | stats count by host`
Results: a handful of parsing warnings on two hosts (auth-edge-02, auth-edge-05) between 03:10-03:22 UTC. No sign of replay or exfil.

ryan: From infra side I'd like to avoid a full package bump if we can hotpatch in a shim or reject the offending token shape at the boundary. But shims at the auth layer could be risky w/ performance.

lena: Proposed triage priority: P1 for production token parsing paths, P2 for batch/worker code paths that only touch token introspection indirectly. Backport if patch is small (<3 LOC) and passes unit tests.

sam: For locking, I suggest we: 1) add an explicit replace directive in root go.mod to the patched commit, 2) add a go vet / module-verify step in CI that fails on unexpected upgrades, and 3) vendor the patched dependency in the Dedicated build.

ada: +1 on vendor for Dedicated builds. Also we should add an audit log entry for any key rotation or KMS access that happens as part of the remedial work. Maria from compliance requested that.

lena: Good catch. We'll coordinate KMS rotations. Question for sec-bot: can we automate an audit log check for any KMS decrypt API calls originating from the deploy user during the hotpatch window?

sec-bot: Automated check available. I can run a daily query and post alerts; for ad-hoc windows we can run a one-off query and attach results to the incident ticket. Runbook: `sec-bot query-kms-activity --since 1765432100 --user=deploy-bot`

ryan: Regarding the backport policy: if the upstream patch is non-api-breaking we should backport to the last LTS branch, otherwise schedule a canary rollout to Dedicated then to Hosted. Canary plan: 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% over 4 hours with automatic rollback on error rate >1%.

sam: CI guard example for module-verify: add this to our CI step:

```bash
go list -m all | grep -E "google.golang.org/grpc|github.com/some/jwtlib" | while read m v; do 
  if ! jq -e ".[\"$m\"] | contains([\"$v\"])" pinned.json >/dev/null; then 
    echo "Dependency mismatch: $m $v not in pinned.json"; exit 1;
  fi
done
```

ada: We should also bump the severity on the vulnerability tracker (internal) to show it affects token parsing. I'll create a ticket IN-9421 and link the logs + repro.

lena: Can someone take a runbook item: assemble hotpatch PR, include a small minimal test that reproduces the parsing warning and a smoke test for auth edge? Assigning to @sam and @ada. ETA 3 hours?

sam: I can do the PR for the shim + replace directive. If backport applies, I'll open a backport PR too.

ada: I'll write the smoke test and add the CI guard.

ryan: I'll schedule the canary and reserve capacity on Dedicated for rollout window. Also will prepare rollback playbook.

lena: For release notes / customer comms: we should prepare a short bulletin saying we patched a dependency that affected token parsing; no evidence of compromise; recommend rotating long-lived tokens as precaution. @maria please review once I draft.

maria: (not in channel) noted — will review.

lena: Summary / action items:
- sam: hotpatch PR + replace in root go.mod (ETA 3h)
- ada: smoke tests + CI guard (ETA 3h)
- ryan: canary schedule + rollback (ETA 4h)
- lena: incident ticket + customer comm draft (ETA 2h)
- sec-bot: run KMS access check during the window

lena: tagging this thread as an incident at IN-9421. If you find anything else flip the channel to #incidents and ping oncall. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Reminder: oncall r2 is @ryan for the next 6h.

sam: Starting work now, will post PR link here when ready.

ada: Tests in progress, a handful of adjustments to mocks.

lena: Thanks team. Keep updates short in this thread.
